title: Finite-basis hypercover existence on a site with fibre products
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a category with fibre products, with possibly distinct object and morphism universes, equipped with any precoverage [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], and let $\mathcal B\subseteq\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal C)$ be a set of objects. Assume every object $T$ has a finite covering $\{B_i\to T\}_{i\in I}$ with all $B_i\in\mathcal B$. Assume also that adjoining one arrow $B\to T$ with $B\in\mathcal B$ to any finite covering with members in $\mathcal B$ again gives a covering. Formal-family index types lie in the maximum of the object and morphism universes. No isomorphism, composition, or base-change axiom on the precoverage is required. Then for each $T\in\mathcal C$ there exists an augmented simplicial object [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-object] $K$ in the category of formal coproducts $\mathrm{SR}(\mathcal C/T)$ [def-weil-pbc-formal-coproduct], with $K_n=\{B_{n,i}\to T\}_{i\in I_n}$, every $I_n$ finite and every $B_{n,i}\in\mathcal B$, whose matching arrows are coverings in every degree. A family morphism $(\alpha,f_i):\{A_i\}\to\{D_j\}$ is a covering here precisely when $\{f_i:A_i\to D_j\mid\alpha(i)=j\}$ covers $D_j$ for each $j$. Matching objects are limits of the compatible proper-face diagram in $\mathrm{SR}(\mathcal C/T)$, with degree-zero matching object the one-member family $\{\operatorname{id}_T\}$. In particular all face and degeneracy maps satisfy the simplicial identities.

proof.text: Fix T and choose a finite B-cover indexed by I. Regard the family of these arrows as a constant zero-truncated simplicial formal family over T. Every index is nondegenerate, and the only zero-simplex operator is the identity, so this truncation is split. The proper-face category in degree zero is empty. The singleton family id_T is terminal among formal families over T and supplies the normalized matching cone. The matching arrow is the chosen cover; its only index fibre gives the same presieve after the surjective reindexing by the singleton fibre.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-site-finite-basis-hypercover-step] recursively to the zero-truncation. The induction invariant includes splitness, finite indices, basis components, normalized degree-zero matching object, limiting proper-face cones with their canonical projections, and componentwise covering matching arrows. Each chosen extension restricts exactly to the preceding truncation. Choice and Nat.rec produce a compatible tower; all choices are local to this existence proof.

For a simplex X define K(X) by evaluating the tower at stage len(X). Transport to any larger stage using the exact restriction equalities. Define the map of an operator at the maximum of its endpoint degrees. Functor.congr_hom of each restriction equality proves independence of the chosen stage. For two composable operators evaluate all three maps at the maximum of the three degrees; functoriality at that stage proves composition. Identities follow in the same way. Functor.ext then proves that the full functor restricts exactly to every stage of the tower.

In degree n use the invariant at the n-th restriction of the assembled functor. Its top term is the degree-n term of K and its proper-face diagram is definitionally the diagram of K. Choose the matching cone and arrow from this invariant in each degree, obtaining all projection equations, IsLimit witnesses and covering presieves simultaneously. Degree zero has the specified singleton point. Objects and morphisms in Over T give the augmentation.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_site_finite_basis_hypercover
    {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] [HasPullbacks C]
    (J : Precoverage C)
    (B : Set C)
    (hcover : ∀ T : C, ∃ (I : Type (max u v)) (U : I → C) (f : ∀ i : I, U i ⟶ T),
      Finite I ∧ (∀ i : I, U i ∈ B) ∧ Presieve.ofArrows U f ∈ J T)
    (hadjoin : ∀ (T : C) (I : Type (max u v)) [Finite I] (U : I → C)
      (f : ∀ i : I, U i ⟶ T), (∀ i : I, U i ∈ B) →
      Presieve.ofArrows U f ∈ J T → ∀ (V : C), V ∈ B → ∀ (g : V ⟶ T),
        Presieve.ofArrows U f ⊔ Presieve.singleton g ∈ J T)
    (T : C) :
    ∃ (K : SimplicialObject (FormalCoproduct.{max u v} (Over T)))
      (M : ∀ n : ℕ, Cone (K.properFaceDiagram n))
      (μ : ∀ n : ℕ, K _⦋n⦌ ⟶ (M n).pt),
      (∀ n : ℕ, Finite (K _⦋n⦌).I) ∧
      (∀ (n : ℕ) (i : (K _⦋n⦌).I), ((K _⦋n⦌).obj i).left ∈ B) ∧
      (M 0).pt = (FormalCoproduct.incl (Over T)).obj (Over.mk (𝟙 T)) ∧
      (∀ n : ℕ, Nonempty (IsLimit (M n))) ∧
      (∀ (n : ℕ) (a : SimplicialObject.ProperFaceCategory n),
        μ n ≫ (M n).π.app (op a) = K.map a.obj.hom.op) ∧
      (∀ (n : ℕ) (j : (M n).pt.I),
        Presieve.ofArrows
          (fun i : {i : (K _⦋n⦌).I // (μ n).f i = j} ↦ ((K _⦋n⦌).obj i.val).left)
          (fun i : {i : (K _⦋n⦌).I // (μ n).f i = j} ↦
            ((μ n).φ i.val).left ≫
              eqToHom (congrArg (fun k ↦ ((M n).pt.obj k).left) i.property)) ∈
          J ((M n).pt.obj j).left)
lean.note: The existing properFaceDiagram is used directly (landed statement dependency added under brief-stage2 §5). Matching cones and their canonical arrows are quantified with IsLimit and the projection equations; covering is the original precoverage condition on each index fibre. Simplicial objects in formal families of Over T carry the augmentation canonically. F2: independent category universes, index universe max u v, and only the used precoverage hypotheses; proof unchanged apart from universe annotations.
